summary: A description of two new commands in UCSB's Simple-Minded File System: Login (LGI), which identifies the user and an account for billing, and Logout (LGO). Users should issue LGI right after the connection setup. Use was not yet billed, but accounting was requested. It was replaced by RFC 431.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 399 adds Login and Logout commands to UCSB's Simple-Minded File System. Login identifies a user and account, while Logout ends that association; RFC 431 later replaced this document.

questions: what do the smfs login and logout commands do
subtitle: Two Simple-Minded File System commands for user identification and accounting

tldr.problem: UCSB's Simple-Minded File System needed commands to identify users and associate their use with an account.
tldr.mechanism: Login records a user name and account number for the connection; Logout ends that accounting association without closing the connection.
tldr.outcome: The commands were optional while use was not billed, and RFC 399 was later replaced by RFC 431.

sections.title: Why Add Login and Logout
sections.content:
RFC 399 describes two commands added to UCSB's Simple-Minded File System (SMFS). Login identifies the user and names the account to which SMFS use is to be billed; Logout ends the association between the user and that accounting information.

At the time of the RFC, SMFS use was not billed and these commands were optional. The document asks users to begin using Login so the system can collect usage statistics before billing is implemented.
sections.plainLanguage: The commands let SMFS record who is using it and which account is associated with the use. They were optional at the time because the system was not billing users.

sections.title: Login and Logout Behavior
sections.content:
A user should issue Login after completing the Initial Connection Protocol and before any command that refers to a file. The user name and account number remain in effect until another Login, a Logout, or connection closure. At the time, the user name could be any name that identified the user and the account number was arbitrary.

Logout ends the accounting association but does not close the connection. After Logout, a user should issue Login before another file operation. The RFC says Logout was optional and did not affect the ability to reference files at that time.
sections.plainLanguage: Login sets the user and account for file activity on the connection. Logout clears that association but leaves the connection open.

sections.title: Command Formats
sections.content:
Login uses opcode 13, followed by a user name and account number. Each field begins with an 8-bit length and contains that many 8-bit characters. The user name can contain at most 8 characters, and the account number at most 4; both use the character set used for file names.

Logout consists of opcode 14 and has no arguments.
sections.plainLanguage: The Login command carries a name and account number, each preceded by its length. Logout is a single opcode with no extra fields.
